## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
visitors <- read_csv("data/UK-visitor-numbers.csv")
#Q1(a)
visitors |> count(region)
#Q1(b)
visitors |> count(admission, setting)
#Q2
visitors |> summarise_all(class)
#Q3
visitors |> arrange(desc(n_2021)) |> head(n=10)
#Q4(d)
visitors |> filter(n_2022 == 565772) #Knowsley Safari and Knowsley Hall
#Q4(e)
visitors |> filter(n_2022 > 1000000) |> count() - 22
#Q5(f)
visitors |> filter(n_2022 > 50000 & n_2022 < 100000) |> count() - 50
#Q5(g)
visitors |> count(region) |> filter(n > 50) #Scotland, 97
```

##Warmup Question Answers
1. "count(visitors)" - 348 attractions
2. attraction - chr, n_2021 - dbl, n_2022 - dbl, admission - chr, setting - chr, region - chr
3. "arrange(visitors, desc(n_2022))" - The Crown Estate, Windsor Great Park
4. "filter(visitors, attraction == "National Museum of Scotland")" - Free
5. "filter(visitors, setting == "O", region == "Yorkshire and the Humber", admission == "Members", n_2022 > "100,000")" - Fountains Abbey Estate, Kirkstall Abbey, RHS Garden Harlow Carr
